opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Undergraduate Tuition Fee Grants

amount.raw: Our grants cover the cost of tuition fees, up to £1,820 per year for a full-time degree course.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Individuals from low-income households who are ineligible for tuition fee support from the Scottish Government; ordinarily resident in Scotland (or with a substantial recent connection); entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK, have Limited Leave to Remain, or be an asylum seeker; enrolled on an undergraduate degree course at an eligible Scottish institution (universities, Glasgow School of Art, Royal Conservatoire of Scotland, SRUC).
opportunities.summary: Grants covering tuition fees (up to £1,820/year) for undergraduate students from low-income households in Scotland who are not eligible for government tuition fee funding, including those returning to study and second-degree reskilling in skills-shortage areas.

opportunities.funder: Carnegie Trust for the Universities of Scotland
opportunities.title: Carnegie-Morgan Scholarship

amount.raw: Full tuition fees for the MSc in Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants plus an additional living-cost bursary of £1,200.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Scottish-domiciled students from low-income households who have been accepted onto the MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants (delivered by Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh and University of Edinburgh), studying full-time or part-time; ordinarily resident in Scotland; entitled to remain indefinitely in the UK; not already holding a postgraduate degree.
opportunities.summary: Scholarship in partnership with the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh covering full tuition fees and a £1,200 living-cost bursary for postgraduate study (MSc Biodiversity and Taxonomy of Plants) to widen participation in plant science and support Scotland's net-zero and biodiversity workforce.
